ledger.claim: The rider's threshold burden opens on a matched record: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the same trip_id, TRP-00113, the trip_record's started_at (2026-08-05T18:47:10+08:00) matches the trace's first fix to the second, and the 20.2 km billed on the ledger corresponds to the 20.18 km the trace itself measures. The first limb of the POL-RD-08 burden is therefore satisfied on the rider's side, so the question is the arithmetic and not the identification of the trip.

The measurement that governs is the trace, not the receipt. POL-RD-01 provides in terms that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree the trace figure governs, and that the rounded trip_record copy may NOT be cited for the threshold test. The distance driven on this trip is therefore the 20.18 km the trace records, and the rider asks the tribunal to fix the measurement on that figure rather than on the 20.2 km convenience copy on the ledger.

The baseline is the platform's matched pooled itinerary, not the rider's solo figure. Because trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL, POL-RD-12 fixes the POL-RD-01 optimal at the matched-itinerary optimal of 19.4 km - the route the platform quoted in the system message timed 18:42:04 and which the rider read at 18:42:31 - and the 15.8 km solo_optimal_distance_km that the rider's own claim compares against is the wrong field, so the rider does not press the 27.8% figure that POL-RD-12 says fails on that ground alone. But POL-RD-12 does no more than set the baseline: it excludes only distance attributable to collecting or setting down the co-rider, and it gives the driver no immunity for excess beyond the matched itinerary, which the clause says is established and refunded as usual where the threshold is crossed.

Measured the way POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-12 require, the excess on this trip is 0.78 km, or 4.02% of the 19.4 km matched itinerary. The rider states plainly that this falls below both POL-RD-01 gates - the 0.8 km absolute threshold and the 20% proportional threshold - and that no route deviation is established on this trip. The rider does not ask the tribunal to find one, because the record will not carry it, and the rider's own 15.8 km framing is not the measure.

I disclose that the only advisory artifact in the bundle is impaired: EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING, its payload is null, its weight_multiplier is 0.0 and the issue code that fired is MISSING_ARTIFACT. Its absence is citable and it is cited here for what it establishes - the bundle carries no traffic advisory covering the Punggol, Hougang or CTE corridors between 18:41 and 19:23 on 5 August 2026, so no POL-RD-03 exoneration of any part of this route is available to the driver, and POL-RD-13 requires any external-cause assertion to be tested against that absent record and nothing else. The driver's explanation on this file is a platform match, not a queue or a closure; it stands or falls on POL-RD-12, and POL-RD-12 sets a baseline rather than excusing excess.

The rider is not a serial claimant, and no adverse inference is available against this claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the heightened corroboration requirement POL-RD-08 imposes on riders with four or more unsubstantiated claims in 60 days is not engaged. Every other field on the rider_profile - prior_disputes_filed, prior_disputes_upheld and the rest - is context only under POL-GEN-01 and may not be used to establish anything about this trip.

ledger.claim: This is a pooled trip, and POL-RD-12 fixes the deviation baseline at the matched-itinerary optimal: the trip record shows vehicle_type RYDE_POOL and an optimal_distance_km of 19.4 for the itinerary actually quoted at match time (Punggol -> Hougang co-rider pickup -> Raffles Place), with solo_optimal_distance_km of 15.8 carried only for reference. The rider's claim measures 20.2 km against the 15.8 km solo figure, which is the wrong field; a claim that measures excess against solo_optimal_distance_km, rather than the matched-itinerary figure, fails on that ground alone. Both figures should be named so the rider can see why: 15.8 km is the unmatched quote, 19.4 km is what the platform quoted for the route driven.

Measured against the correct baseline, no deviation is established. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement and expressly forbids citing the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test; the trace figure is 20.18 km against the 19.4 km optimal, an excess of 0.78 km, or 4.02%. Both establishment gates must pass and neither does: 0.78 km is below the 0.8 km absolute threshold and 4.02% is far below the 20% relative threshold. Where either test fails, POL-RD-01 states the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The Hougang leg the rider complains of is the platform-matched co-rider pickup, not a detour the driver chose. POL-RD-12 excludes distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary from excess before POL-RD-01 is applied, and the driver's recorded message in the chat log is to the same effect: 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route'. The 90-second stop the driver's trace shows at Hougang is that pickup, and it is never counted as deviation.

The rider was notified of the pooled route and its distance before the trip began. The platform's own match notification MSG-00113-001, sent at 18:42:04 and read at 18:42:31, states 'Co-rider matched. Your pooled route now includes one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min'. The rider therefore accepted a 19.4 km pooled itinerary, and the 20.18 km actually driven is 0.78 km from that quoted figure, not the 4.4 km the claim implies.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, from an unimpaired trace, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold. The trace here is unimpaired - 100% coverage, 217 fixes, no gaps, admissibility COMPLETE at weight 1.0 - and it yields an excess of 0.78 km, below both gates. The burden therefore never shifts to the driver, and no exculpatory clause under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 needs to be invoked at all.

No material deviation arises on this trip: the excess of 0.78 km is far below the 50% / 8.0 km material thresholds in POL-RD-01, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is never engaged. For completeness on that check, the driver's trailing figures are deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 471 - no repeat-deviation pattern exists, and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral can follow from this trip.

There is nothing on the fare to refund under POL-RD-09: the fare is the METERED $26.83, erp_gantries is empty and tolls_erp is 0.00, airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and a $3.00 pool discount has already been applied. There is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge, so no billing-integrity correction is available; and because no deviation is established under POL-RD-01, the POL-RD-02 recomputation does not run at all.

The correct outcome is NO_ACTION, and under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative and preserves the present payment state. On this rider-filed dispute the fare is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd at 0.00, so NO_ACTION leaves the $26.83 charge standing in full - which is precisely the result the driver seeks and which no clause in this policy displaces.

The driver asserts no external traffic cause - no queue, closure or incident - so no traffic excuse is before the tribunal and the absent advisory is immaterial. The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING (status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, so it can carry no fact), and its absence cannot be turned against the driver because the driver does not rely on POL-RD-03 or on any advisory. The driver's explanation is the platform's own co-rider match, established by the trip record and the chat log, not by any road condition.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the measurements, and the record supports that agreement. This was a RYDE_POOL trip. Under POL-RD-12 the correct baseline is the matched-itinerary optimal on the trip record, 19.4 km, not the 15.8 km solo figure the rider's claim used; the rider's 15.8 km comparison is the wrong field and fails on that ground. Under POL-RD-01 the GPS trace governs the actual distance: EV-GPS-00113 records 20.18 km. The excess over the matched 19.4 km itinerary is therefore 0.78 km, or 4.02%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only when the excess is both more than 0.8 km and more than 20% of the optimal. The excess is below both gates, so no route deviation is established. The Hougang stop is the platform-matched co-rider pickup, not a driver-chosen detour: the system notification MSG-00113-001 at 18:42:04 quoted the pooled 19.4 km route, and POL-RD-12 excludes co-rider collection distance from the excess. There is no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.00, airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither starts nor ends at an airport, and the $3.00 pool discount is already applied to the $26.83 charged. No POL-RD-06 conduct referral is triggered because there is no material deviation and no repeat-deviation pattern: the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 471 completed trips in 90 days. The rider's profile also shows no serial-claimant factor under POL-RD-08. The outcome is NO_ACTION: the $6.00 contested amount and the $26.83 charge stand, with no refund and no driver compensation.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
